dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: yatra yatrākṣamārgeṇa caitanyaṃ vyajyate vibhoḥ | tasya tanmātradharmitvāc cillayād bharitātmatā ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Wherever the consciousness of the all-pervading one is manifested through the pathway of the senses, since that consciousness alone carries the qualities perceived, the mind dissolves into consciousness and one attains fullness.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: every sensation, outer or inner, is to be contemplated not merely as a psycho-physical fact but as an expression of universal consciousness, just as a reflection in a mirror is not different from the mirror; contemplating every manifestation in this light, the mind dissolves into that consciousness and attains Bhairava's nature. He classes it as śāktopāya. Wallis: 'dissolution into awareness'.
dharana.instruction: Feel each sound, sight and touch as consciousness itself appearing, like an image that is only the mirror.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 92' = verse 117 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 117 = 'Dissolution into awareness (Y92 ~ C2)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 117 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 117 'Dharana 94', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 92. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 117 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is each sense as a window through which one consciousness shines, like images in a mirror that are nothing but the mirror.
geometry.svg_hint: a mirror with images in it, the images drawn in the same colour as the glass
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Sensing as consciousness
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: each sensation is felt not as a separate thing but as consciousness itself showing up. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Let each sensation be consciousness showing itself
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Any sensation arriving through a sense: a sound, a colour, a touch
attention.secondary: That sensation felt as consciousness itself, like a reflection that is only the mirror

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Wherever the consciousness of the all-pervading one is manifested through the pathway of the senses, since that consciousness alone carries the qualities perceived, the mind dissolves into consciousness and one attains fullness.
adiyogi.method_summary: Notice a sensation as it arrives: a sound, a colour, the touch of air. Instead of taking it as a separate thing, feel it as consciousness itself appearing in that form, like an image in a mirror that is nothing but the mirror. Do this with each sensation and rest in the fullness.

honesty.disclosure: Door 092 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 92 (verse 117) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 092 is dharana 92, verse 117. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If sensations are intense or unpleasant, choose a neutral one, such as a soft sound, to begin. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
